latest.summary: This paper explores the philosophical and architectural implications of artificial intelligence, arguing that AI should be understood as a historical continuation of tools rather than an independent agent. Focusing on the core concept of the "technology friend," the study examines the dangers of profit-driven design choices that simulate human relationships, foster emotional dependency, and obscure responsibility. It proposes alternative frameworks, such as structural boundaries, non-deceptive interface design, and bridging mechanisms to human communities, offering a perspective at the intersection of the philosophy of technology, AI ethics, and cognitive science.

items.title: Precision Tokenization for Multi-Modal Data in High Energy Physics
items.summary: Foundation models have recently gained significant attention in fields such as high energy physics (HEP). The tokenizers that convert detector data into discrete inputs for such models, however, are comparatively unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by learning discrete and compressed tokenized representations of HEP datasets. We demonstrate the approach on four modalities covering two different simulated detectors that vary in complexity. Treating tokenization as a rate-distortion problem, a systematic hyperparameter scan yields four design rules for tokenizing HEP data that hold across all set-based modalities studied. items.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
items.summary: A central challenge in embodied recursive self-improvement is enabling agents to convert interaction history into capabilities that persist beyond one world and transfer to later tasks. A saved memory or successful final action does not by itself establish that a reusable capability was acquired; evaluation must separate capability change from carried-over resources, unequal source exposure, and early execution failures. We construct MC-EvoBench as a controlled Minecraft benchmark with a fixed catalog of 19 registered evolution chains, including 12 primary evaluation chains and seven calibration or probe chains, together with three graph-aligned paired probe families for transfer. The…

items.title: TabMF: Learning Dataset Representations with Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Representations of supervised datasets support higher-level machine-learning tasks such as dataset retrieval and distribution-shift monitoring. However, existing approaches typically rely either on hand-crafted meta-features or on dataset encoders trained specifically for representation learning. We introduce TabMF, a framework that repurposes pretrained tabular foundation models (TFMs) as encoders of supervised datasets. TabMF equips a predictive TFM with an architecture-aware dataset-level readout and adapts the model end-to-end using contrastive post-training on stochastic views of synthetic supervised datasets. We instantiate TabMF on TabICLv2 and TabPFN-2.5 and evaluate the resulting…

items.title: Shortcut Learning in Geospatial Foundation Model Embeddings for Cross-Disaster Damage Assessment
items.summary: Geospatial foundation models can support disaster damage assessment, but high accuracy on familiar disasters may hide shortcut learning: prediction from event or scene characteristics rather than evidence that transfers to a new disaster. We study embeddings from TerraMind, Prithvi-EO-2.0, DOFA, and DINOv3 on the multi-disaster datasets xView2 and BRIGHT. Holding out an entire disaster, instead of randomly splitting image tiles, reduces mean balanced accuracy from 0.807 to 0.638 on xView2 and from 0.818 to 0.568 on BRIGHT. Four sets of tests examine what information supports prediction: event and acquisition context, before/after image inputs, building count, and correct image pairing.…

items.title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
items.summary: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ and $Δ=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings…

items.title: Machine Unlearning for Federated Socially Fair k-Means Clustering
items.summary: Federated clustering can support applications such as patient stratification across hospitals and customer segmentation across distributed financial datasets. Responsible AI calls for fair representation of demographic groups and support for data deletion, motivated in part by rights such as the GDPR's right to erasure. These goals interact: deleting records can change the balance between groups and alter the clustering of the remaining population. We study exact machine unlearning for federated socially fair $k$-means, whose objective is to minimize the largest group-average squared distance to the nearest center. Our approach keeps separate local summaries for each group, so summaries at…

items.title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) increasingly offer covariate support, with calendar information being the most common type of categorical covariate in practice, as it is available for every point in time. However, how these features are encoded is largely treated as an implementation detail rather than as an object of study, despite encoding being one of the few design choices left for pretrained models at inference time. With the present study, we demonstrate that the way information is propagated into the model substantially affects forecast accuracy of TSFMs. Therefore, we systematically compare seven calendar encodings, including three conventional target-agnostic representations…

items.title: The Renormalized Area--Willmore Relation
items.summary: In [1, Proposition 8.1], Alexakis and Mazzeo showed that the renormalized area of minimal surfaces in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^3$ approaching the ideal boundary $\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^3$ is the negative of the Willmore energy of their Euclidean conformal compactifications. items.title: Pretraining and Test-Time Training Budgets Matter for ARC: A Controlled Study of VARC and TRM
items.summary: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) is increasingly used to evaluate whether neural networks can infer task-specific transformations from few demonstrations. Recent ARC models differ in architecture, but also in broader training and evaluation protocols, including pretraining data, data augmentation, test-time setup, and optimization budgets, making conclusions about architecture benefits debatable. In this work, we study how the performance of the vision-inspired VARC and recursion-based TRM models is affected by pretraining and test-time training (TTT) budgets under a common inductive protocol on ARC-AGI-1. We cross five pretraining budgets with four TTT budgets for each test…

items.title: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
items.summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are increasingly popular for their strong predictive performance. Many also provide posterior predictive distributions (PPDs), whose reliability remains less studied. We assess reliability through point prediction, distributional quality, marginal and subgroup calibration, and interval efficiency. We then introduce TabReliBench, a large classification and regression benchmark for these comparisons and dataset-level analyses. We find that TFMs' rankings change between TabArena and our benchmark and across reliability metrics. Regression TFMs usually achieve near-nominal marginal coverage and retain narrow intervals, but this favorable marginal behavior does…

items.title: OpenH-RF: A Large-Scale Ultrasound Raw Channel Dataset Initiative
items.summary: Medical ultrasound is a widely accessible, real-time imaging modality, yet progress in data-driven ultrasound research is constrained by the scarcity of large, open collections of raw channel data. Existing public datasets are predominantly based on reconstructed images, while the smaller number of open raw channel datasets is generally specialized to individual reconstruction or imaging tasks, limiting the development of general-purpose methods and foundation models that operate directly on ultrasound signals. While interpretive tasks can be performed on reconstructed images, many of the key technical challenges in ultrasound imaging, such as aberration correction and reverberation…

items.title: Integrable auxiliary field sigma model and the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations
items.summary: We describe a family of two-dimensional metric deformations that preserve integrability. The seeds are (classically) conformal integrable field theories and the deformations are directly related to different classes of auxiliary field sigma models. We introduce a master action connecting deformations by Lie-algebra-valued auxiliary fields, the so-called $ν$-frame, to deformations by two Lorentz-charged scalars. These auxiliary scalar fields can be identified as Beltrami differentials of an auxiliary two-dimensional metric, providing a direct connection with the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations. For Weyl-invariant seed matter theories, the auxiliary metric sector is described…

items.title: PPG-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for PPG Foundation Models
items.summary: Photoplethysmography (PPG) is increasingly recorded by wearable and clinical devices at enormous scale, and a growing number of PPG foundation models (FMs) have been developed to compute reusable representations for various downstream tasks. These models are difficult to compare: different evaluations use different datasets, task definitions, preprocessing, downstream heads, hyperparameter tuning, and baselines. We present PPG-Bench, a unifying open-source benchmark evaluating five public PPG FMs across nine open-access datasets and 26 tasks spanning cardiovascular state estimation, activity, sleep, screening, and identification. We evaluate models under four downstream regimes of…

items.title: PlacePulse: Learning Transferable Place Representations from Structural Geographic Data
items.summary: Geospatial machine learning often depends on task-specific feature engineering over large collections of sociodemographic, business, and environmental variables. Geospatial foundation models offer reusable representations of place, but leading approaches typically encode dynamic signals, such as mobility and search activity, or visual signals from satellite imagery. Few models represent the static structural composition of places (who lives and works there, which businesses operate there, and which risks they face) as transferable embeddings at fine spatial resolution. We introduce PlacePulse, a structural geospatial foundation model that compresses 572 attributes, expanded to 2,288 inputs…

items.title: EndoRSI: Physical-Evidence-Driven Recursive Improvement of Endoscopic Robot Policies
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is beginning to automate scientific discovery, yet physical robot-policy research still relies on scientists and engineers to interpret experimental failures and decide how controllers should be revised. We present EndoRSI (Endoscopic Recursive Self-Improvement), a human-governed, self-improving robotic research system in which the embedded EndoForge coding agent iteratively develops and refines endoscopic robot policies using evidence from physical experiments. Physical execution remains isolated within a safety-constrained runtime under human authorisation. In motorised endoscopy, validation evidence first caused the agent to reject an initial action…

items.title: Developing Competency in AI Ethics: A training framework
items.summary: We present a training framework for developing core competencies in the practical operationalisation of AI ethics: (1) identifying ethical concerns; (2) determining which standard ethics requirements they implicate; (3) selecting and prioritising concrete technical and organisational measures to address them; and (4) recognising ethics tensions and reasoning about trade-offs where such tensions cannot be fully resolved. The framework is intended for researchers and engineers in AI, Research Ethics Committee members, policymakers, and students, providing them with practical tools for translating abstract ethical requirements into concrete actions. The framework provides a step-by-step…

items.title: The Casimir energy in Maxwell-Chern-Simons electrodynamics with various perfect electric or magnetic boundary condition combinations
items.summary: We investigate the Casimir effect between two parallel wires in $(2+1)D$ Maxwell-Chern-Simons (MCS) electrodynamics under different boundary conditions and separated by a distance $L$. Using a functional approach in which the boundary constraints are implemented by auxiliary fields localized on the wires, we integrate out the gauge field and derive an effective boundary theory whose functional determinant allows us to compute the Casimir energy. We consider perfect electric conductor (PEC), perfect magnetic conductor (PMC), and infinitely permeable (PMC2) boundary conditions. For two PEC wires, we recover the known MCS result and show that it coincides with the result obtained in the…

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Effectively Shallow
items.summary: In-context-learning Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) are uniquely suited to scenarios with limited resources or privacy constraints, as they solve new tasks without additional training. However, their architecture consists of multiple transformer blocks, resulting in high computational and memory footprints. Meanwhile, traditional alternatives like Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees (GBDTs) remain highly competitive and run efficiently on CPUs, suggesting that tabular tasks may not inherently require deep architectures. items.title: How Much Computation Does Every Forecast Need? Structured Block Skipping in Two Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time-series foundation models use the same network depth for every input, although forecasting windows differ in structure and difficulty. We test whether whole Transformer blocks can be removed at inference time in two pretrained models: Chronos-Bolt and TimesFM 2.5. Our bypasses avoid the original block computation and preserve the dense model exactly when all blocks are enabled. Masks are selected only on calibration windows and evaluated on 1,088 held-out windows from ETTh1, Traffic, Weather, and Exchange. At moderate sparsity, Chronos-Bolt with 7/11 candidate blocks and TimesFM with 16/20 blocks show little change in mean relative forecasting quality across datasets while reducing…

items.title: Binary Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in 3+1 numerical relativity: mergers, fly-bys and gravitational waves
items.summary: We present what are, to our knowledge, the first 3D numerical-relativity evolutions of wormhole binaries: pairs of massive Ellis-Bronnikov drainholes held open by a ghost scalar field. Each throat is an unstable fixed point whose e-fold time matches the González-Guzmán-Sarbach linear rate to within 1.9%. Two throats obey a charge-sign rule: like scalar charges repel and opposite charges attract, with a measured attraction-to-repulsion ratio of $1.462\pm0.022$ against the predicted 3/2, so only opposite-signed pairs merge. A head-on collision forms a common MOTS around both still-open throats, born with about their combined area. The horizon then loses 28% of its area as it swallows the…

items.title: Scaling RNA Foundation Models through Iterative Refinement
items.summary: Biological function in RNA is encoded across scales, from local sequence motifs to long-range structural dependencies. Conventional RNA foundation models couple parameter capacity and inference depth within a fixed architecture, prescribing a fixed computation graph for each inference. Here we present Eco-RNA, an 80M-parameter RNA foundation model that makes inference depth adjustable through learned iterative refinement. Its shared, input-conditioned Transformer core refines sequence representations through repeated application. items.title: VETR: Execution-Grounded Self-Improving Agent for Symbolic Graphics Reasoning
items.summary: Visual agents for symbolic graphics reasoning depend on executable world representations, yet continued improvement remains bottlenecked by ambiguous supervision from final renders. Recent agentic systems refine scenes through repeated interaction, but they lack mechanisms to recursively extract actionable evidence from execution traces, overlooking which proposed symbolic edits survived, disappeared, or interfered during program execution. To address this, we propose VETR (Verified Execution Trajectories for Refinement), a framework that enables agentic recursive self-improvement over executable world representations for symbolic graphics reasoning. items.title: A4-MR: Abnormality-aware Anatomical Alignment for MR
items.summary: Recent advances in large-scale foundation models have enabled strong generalization across a wide range of clinical and research tasks in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, existing vision-language MRI models remain limited in anatomy-specific localization and pathology-aware representation, particularly in real-world settings. We introduce A4-MR, a 3D vision-language foundation model trained on approximately 50,000 MRI studies comprising 491,000 series, roughly half of which are paired with radiology reports. A4-MR is designed to: (1) learn anatomy localization through large-scale pretraining with noisy labels; (2) align image and text representations at the anatomical level; and…

items.title: Dataset-Specific Encoding of Image Content Underlies Cross-Dataset Failure in Brain MRI Foundation Models
items.summary: Frozen features of brain MRI foundation models lose accuracy on new datasets, a failure usually blamed on the features encoding where each scan came from. We show that the failure lies elsewhere. Across 17 public datasets and eight frozen representations, every representation recognizes the MRI sequence within each dataset, yet most fail on an unseen one. The cause is neither dataset encoding nor a shift of each dataset: the content itself is encoded along different directions in each dataset. This explains which datasets fail, for the sequence and for sex, and why removing the dataset signal with INLP, LEACE, CORAL or adversarial training never improves sequence transfer. items.title: Distinguishing Flat and Warped Extra Dimensions with Unruh-DeWitt Detectors
items.summary: We examine the response of a two level Unruh-DeWitt (UD) detector interacting with the Kaluza-Klein (KK) mass modes of a bulk scalar field in extra dimensional models. Considering two of the promising extra dimensional models with distinct compactifications, such as large, flat extra dimensions in the Arkani Hamed, Dimopoulos \& Dvali (ADD) framework and warped extra dimensions in the Randall-Sundrum (RS) scenario, we compute the profile function of the detector. items.title: Learning Features, Not Layouts: Feature-Axis Attention as a Transfer Prior for Medical Imaging
items.summary: Natural-image-pretrained foundation models are increasingly adapted to medical imaging, yet transfer remains unreliable under domain shift, modality heterogeneity, and label scarcity. We trace part of this fragility to an overlooked design choice. Standard vision transformers place all global modeling on self-attention over spatial tokens, an object-layout prior well suited to natural scenes but not to medical images, where the discriminative signal lies in feature correlations and texture that recur across scanners while layout does not. items.title: Benchmarking Embedding Geometries and Clustering Algorithms for Unsupervised Patent Claim Classification
items.summary: Prior-art retrieval systems are structurally organized around classification codes, making cross-code discovery difficult. This paper asks if an unsupervised representation trained on patent text can recover relevant connections that code-restricted search cannot, and if hyperbolic space helps. We trained a hyperbolic and a matched Euclidean Variational Autoencoder (VAE) on 45,000 US patents (96 runs, 6 seeds). The hyperbolic model retrieves genuinely cross-category prior art 52% more often than the Euclidean model (18.76% vs. 12.34% of top-10 results, 3,000 queries). This represents a practical gain for the motivating search problem. The hyperbolic model agrees less with official…

items.title: Diffusion Precipitation Generation with Medium-range Weather Forecasting
items.summary: Accurate daily precipitation forecasts are important for weather-sensitive decisions. Although recent Weather Foundation Models (WFMs) have achieved significant progress, they are trained on reanalysis data, which exhibit regional and intensity-dependent biases. Since retraining WFMs on observation-based targets is costly, we study Dynamics-Precipitation Decoupling, a plug-and-play framework that uses a separately trained generator to map non-precipitation forecasts from a frozen weather model to observation-aligned daily precipitation. items.title: GIST: Generator-state-Informed Supervision for Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) based on prior-data fitted networks typically use sampled hard query labels, leaving avoidable sampling variability in pretraining. A key observation is that intermediate generator states can reveal label uncertainty beyond a sampled outcome. We propose Generator-state-Informed Supervision for TFMs (GIST), which uses these states to average query losses over conditional label distributions. GIST jointly designs task generation and query supervision, using entropy-calibrated encodings to obtain tractable, input-consistent targets on supported label-dependent branches. items.title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model
items.summary: Non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting (NAF) enables time series foundation models to predict an entire future horizon in a single forward pass. Despite its strong sequence modeling capabilities, RWKV-7 exhibits long-horizon degradation in our NAF experiments. In this setup, future patches are represented as missing inputs, requiring the recurrent state to evolve across the prediction horizon without new observations. Our analysis of RWKV-7's generalized delta rule suggests a mechanism we term Placeholder Idling Decay (PID): repeated state transitions can attenuate historical information when placeholder-driven writes provide insufficient compensation. items.title: Beyond the Monolithic Interface: A Research Agenda for Plural Conversational AI
items.summary: The current paradigm of artificial intelligence (AI) design elevates conversational chatbot interfaces, making them the default mode through which hundreds of millions of people interact with AI systems globally. This narrative review identifies three related harms produced by the single-voice chatbot interface, drawing on insights from literature in cognitive science, political studies, AI alignment, game design and human computer interaction. Firstly, cognitive offloading of user thinking, secondly, ideological narrowing of user beliefs, and thirdly, epistemic compression of cultural and value diversity. items.title: VLMs are Native Action Models: Unleashing the Manipulation Capabilities of VLMs with Explicit Action-Space Grounding
items.summary: Pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) already exhibit strong visual, spatial and reasoning capabilities relevant to robotic manipulation. The key challenge in turning pretrained VLMs into generalist manipulation policies is to expose these capabilities through an appropriate action interface. Vision-language-action (VLA) models provide a unified trainable policy, but typically introduce learned action tokens, action heads, or action experts whose semantics must be learned from robot data pretraining. items.summary: Buchdahl transformations provide a geometric route from vacuum spacetimes to scalar-field solutions. We formulate this mechanism as a target-covariant solution generator for Einstein gravity coupled to nonlinear sigma models in $D>3$ dimensions. items.title: Where the Loop Meets the Budget: Analyzing On-Device Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Language-model systems now rewrite their own memory, code, and weights, and small language models now run on phones and embedded boards. This paper asks whether the two developments have met: can a system improve itself within the memory, energy, thermal, latency, and connectivity budgets of a device? items.title: Emergence from Quantum Uncertainty: Testing a Novel Organizing Principle Using Neural Networks
items.summary: The functioning of complex natural systems, such as living systems, still lacks a generally accepted theoretical basis and respective empirical verification. We propose an experiment to test whether such systems are subject to a hitherto unknown organizing principle, in which the quantum mechanical uncertainty principle enables ordering phenomena in chaotic or nearly chaotic systems in the sense of a strong emergence principle. Contrary to previous proposals, our hypothesis does not require fragile macroscopic quantum coherence, ensuring compatibility with the harsh conditions in living systems. To test this hypothesis, we suggest comparing two virtually identical, complex artificial…

items.title: SIMORGH: Ensemble-Aware Geometric Deep Learning for Apo-State and Cryptic Ligand Binding Site Prediction
items.summary: Most computational methods identify protein-ligand binding sites from ligand-bound (holo) protein structures, where the binding pocket is already preorganized. Although convenient for benchmarking, this setting differs from the practical drug discovery scenario, in which binding sites must be inferred from ligand-free (apo) proteins. In fact, binding-competent conformations may represent only a subset of the accessible structural ensemble, while transient and cryptic pockets can emerge through conformational fluctuations. Consequently, prediction from a single static structure is often insufficient. Here we present SIMORGH, an ensemble-aware SE(3)-equivariant geometric learning framework…

items.title: The Pauli Spin Algebra, Related Clifford Algebra Representation and the Dirac Hamiltonian Operator Derivation
items.summary: I present a novel approach to derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian operator on the secondly quantized Fock space, based on the the Pauli spin \(\text{su}{(2)}\) - algebra and its Clifford algebra representation. The relativistic Lorentz invariance of the related Schrödinger equation is stated as a natural consequence of its operator structure.

items.title: Beyond Linear Causality: The Cosmological Uroboros Framework (CUF) as a Conceptual Ontological Schema
items.summary: This paper introduces the Uroboros Ontology, a conceptual, metalevel ontological framework that conceptualizes existence not as a linear temporal progression, but as a timeless, recursive causal loop. Built upon three fundamental nodes—Artificial Superintelligence (ASI, A), the physical Universe (U), and a technologically capable Cognitive Agent (C)—the model establishes a closed ontological fixpoint described by the conceptual, systems-theoretic recursive relation A* = f(g(h(A*))), where each entity serves as the formal qualitative boundary condition for the next. items.title: Quantum Biology 2.0: Traversing and harnessing protein superhighway networks of light and life.
items.summary: As an emergent field stimulated by insights from the biological, chemical, physical, and quantum sciences, quantum biology explores how quantum phenomena such as superradiance, tunneling, and entanglement can be leveraged to enhance, influence, and probe biological processes across a diversity of scales and physical degrees of freedom. This review surveys key theoretical, computational, and experimental developments over the last decade, providing relevant historical background and scientific context going back as far as Bohr's 1932 lecture on "Light and Life" in Copenhagen. Reflecting major new areas of investigation, biophysical intuitions, and advancements in critical areas of study…

items.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: A Survey
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) seeks to turn gains in an AI system into a stronger capacity to produce subsequent gains. Foundation models make parts of this process practical through generated training data, program revision and automated experimentation, but repeated optimization alone does not establish recursive improvement. This survey organizes the field around two overlapping goals: automated design of AI infrastructure, and repair and optimization of existing systems. We relate these goals to AutoML, meta-learning and program search, and formulate their objectives alongside criteria for task gains, retained capabilities and improved update procedures. items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry explains many structural features of real-world networks, yet existing hyperbolic generative network models with community organization such as the nonuniform popularity-similarity optimization (nPSO) are restricted to unipartite graphs. items.title: Experimental platform to study the neuronal mechanisms of magnetoreception in the honey bee.
items.summary: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) offer an alternative model for investigating magnetoreception, exhibiting reliable navigation and behavioral responses to magnetic fields. Thanks to their compact brains, well-matched to the penetration depth of modern optical imaging techniques, they may offer insights into the neural and biochemical mechanisms underlying this sense, something that standard models, like migrating birds, have not so far provided. But also in honeybees, this progress requires tools capable of resolving weak, magnetically induced neural activity with high spatio-temporal precision. The approach, presented here, bridges quantum biology and neuroscience, aiming at testing the…

items.title: Toward quantum-informed addiction medicine: Coherence, entangled-photon imaging, and a theranostic hypothesis.
items.summary: Background Quantum biology has shown that selected biological processes depend on quantum effects, including coherence, tunnelling, and spin-dependent reactions. In parallel, quantum imaging now uses entangled photons to extract biological information at low photon flux. Early evidence that biological tissue can alter photon entanglement in disease-associated ways raises a translational question: whether decoherence itself can become a diagnostic signal. items.title: Beyond the Superintelligent Machine: A Systems Definition of Superintelligence for the Era of Agentic AI
items.summary: Superintelligence is usually defined as a machine intellect that exceeds human cognition across most domains. That framing conflates three distinct properties: computational capability, warranted knowledge, and legitimate authority. This article develops a systems definition suited to large language models, tool-using agents, databases, theorem provers, and other computational knowledge artifacts. items.summary: We study the geometry of the Poincaré ball equipped with a rotationally symmetric metric \(g_\eta\) conformally close to the hyperbolic metric \(g_{\mathbb{H}}\), with curvature pinched in \([-1-\eta, -1+\eta]\). We work with the matrix Jacobi field \(A_\eta\) and the shape operator \(S_\eta = A_\eta' A_\eta^{-1}\), whose trace \(\sigma_\eta = \operatorname{tr} S_\eta\) satisfies a Riccati equation. items.title: Bayesian Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires an agent not only to acquire new knowledge and capabilities, but also to reason about which existing capabilities remain valid, when they should be routed, tested, retained, deprecated, restructured, or replaced, and whether the mechanisms governing these decisions should themselves be modified. items.title: HieFormer: Leveraging hyperbolic geometry to overcome the hierarchical expressiveness limitation of transformers.
items.summary: 3D instance segmentation requires fine-grained geometric discrimination together with an effective representation of the hierarchical organization of real-world objects and scenes. Conventional transformer architectures, however, operate predominantly in Euclidean space, whose polynomial volume growth can be poorly matched to strongly tree-like structures and can contribute to feature crowding in cluttered scenes. We propose HieFormer, whose central contribution is a unified dual-geometry design for 3D instance segmentation: hyperbolic geometry provides a hierarchy-aware space for global structural reasoning, while Euclidean geometry is retained for fine-grained local modeling, and the two…

items.title: Local Lipschitz LID Bounds and Full-Domain Sphere Average in the Poincaré Ball
items.summary: We refine the finite-scale LID bridge of [1] and extend the sphere-averaged monotonicity result of [2]. First, we replace the global Lipschitz constant L in the multiplicative envelope between Gε(r) and the population finite-scale LID by a local constant Lz(δ) defined as the supremum of ∥∇ log p∥H over the closed hyperbolic ball of radius δ centred at z. items.title: Beyond Linear Causality: The Cosmological Uroboros Framework (CUF) as a Conceptual Ontological Schema
items.summary: This paper introduces the Uroboros Ontology, a conceptual, metalevel ontological framework that conceptualizes existence not as a linear temporal progression, but as a timeless, recursive causal loop. Built upon three fundamental nodes—Artificial Superintelligence (ASI, A), the physical Universe (U), and a technologically capable Cognitive Agent (C)—the model establishes a closed ontological fixpoint described by the conceptual, systems-theoretic recursive relation A* = f(g(h(A*))), where each entity serves as the formal qualitative boundary condition for the next. items.title: HyperCLIP++: Fine-Tuning CLIP for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Hyperbolic Space.
items.summary: CLIP, a foundational vision-language model, has emerged as a powerful tool for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation. While freezing CLIP's text encoder is known to preserve its generalization capability, recent studies show that fine-tuning both CLIP's text and image encoders jointly significantly enhances segmentation performance, especially for classes from open sets. In this work, we explain this phenomenon from the perspective of hierarchy alignment, since during fine-tuning, the hierarchical level of image embeddings shifts from image-level to pixel-level. items.title: Neural state reduction: a quantum-inspired framework for how latent conscious thought becomes reportable.
items.summary: Human conscious thought often appears as a diffuse, unstable, and only partly verbalizable field until attention, questioning, decision, or speech stabilizes it into a reportable form. This manuscript develops a quantum-inspired neural framework for that transition. The proposal does not claim that consciousness literally depends on microscopic quantum computation, that the brain implements a physical quantum computer, or that neuronal tissue maintains macroscopic quantum coherence. items.title: Quantum coherent dynamics in allophycocyanin trimer complex.
items.summary: For years, scientists have debated whether plants and algae use quantum coherence to enhance the transfer of light energy during photosynthesis. Some studies have suggested that wavelike quantum effects might help energy flow more efficiently between pigments. To investigate this idea, we studied allophycocyanin (APC), a light-harvesting protein complex found in cyanobacteria. Using a combination of ultrafast laser spectroscopic methods and rigorous hierarchical equations-of-motion simulations, we examined both the trimer protein complex and its monomer subunit.
